status: pre-registered after smokes (part A: block 17, 512 neurons, 47 prompts; part B: French items only), before the full runs
question: Gemini 4's reading of e670 against e673: a neuron's activation dies at its token but its write direction persists, so the write dictionary is a cross-position forensic trace that, given only a summary state, recovers which upstream neurons wrote its content at earlier tokens. e670's echo ranked rows against a pole difference built from many labelled items; the claim is label-free and per state.
design: Part A: Pythia-410m, e568's 280 prompts, blocks 12, 17, 22, all 4,096 neurons; each neuron zeroed at every position before the last; damage = absolute drop in log p of the model's own top-1 token at the last position (primary) and KL; predictors: projection of the final state (after the block, and the last layer's state, centred over prompts) on the unit write direction (activation-free), the earlier positions' write size, gradient x activation over earlier positions (absolute sum; absolute signed sum), the final-position activation; Spearman across neurons, bootstrap over neurons. Part B: Qwen2.5-0.5B, e670's translation items (French, Spanish, German), gender and number; each item's final-position state at block 12, centred over all items, projected on every MLP write row of blocks 0-12 (no labels); the oracle rows' ranks; per held-out item its own top 32 rows negated, flips against e670's supervised echo top 32, the oracle's top 32 and 32 random rows.

hypotheses.F1: Gemini's trace, part A: at each block the activation-free projection of the final state ranks neurons by their cross-position damage at Spearman 0.3 or more (either state)
hypotheses.F2: part A: the projection predicts cross-position damage better than the earlier positions' write size (bootstrap 95% CI of the difference above 0) at each block
hypotheses.F3: part B: negating each held-out marked item's own top 32 rows by its label-free projection flips at least half as many items as e670's supervised echo, for gender and for number
hypotheses.F4: part B: the attribute's oracle top row ranks in the top 100 of 63,232 rows under the label-free projection for at least half of the items, for gender and for number
